protocol_messiah_complex_succession.business_logic: Succession Pressure & The Heir Apparent Problem
protocol_messiah_complex_succession.application: Succession planning, leadership development programs, heir apparent management, expectation setting, distributed leadership models
protocol_messiah_complex_succession.narrative: First mutant baby born since M-Day becomes instant flashpoint. X-Men want to protect her. Purifiers want to kill her. Marauders want to kidnap her. Government wants to control her. Cable steals her, escapes to future to raise her as warrior (becomes Hope Summers). Every faction sees the baby differently: savior, threat, weapon, symbol. The "messiah" label creates impossible expectations. She's simultaneously salvation and target.
protocol_messiah_complex_succession.business_translation: Chelsea Clinton, kids of tech founders, Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia. The "next generation" leader bears impossible expectations. Every stakeholder projects different hopes/fears. Groomed for succession but pressure creates dysfunction. The role of savior is toxic. Many heirs apparent fail or reject the burden entirely.

dimensions.title: Succession Pressure Psychology
dimensions.analysis: Growing up as "the one" creates identity distortion. No normal childhood, only preparation. High rates of substance abuse, mental health issues in heirs.
dimensions.metric: Heir apparent psychological health - mental health outcomes for designated successors vs. siblings/peers without succession burden.

dimensions.title: Grooming Systems & Leadership Development
dimensions.analysis: The technical infrastructure of creating leaders. Executive training programs, rotation through divisions, board observation. Sometimes works; often creates entitlement without competence.
dimensions.metric: Successor readiness gap - assessed capability vs. role requirements at succession moment.

dimensions.title: Succession Market Dynamics
dimensions.analysis: When succession is telegraphed, markets price it in. Smooth transition = no reaction. Unexpected change = volatility. The baby's existence changes mutant political economics immediately.
dimensions.metric: Succession announcement impact - stock price/market reaction to heir apparent designation vs. unexpected successor.

dimensions.title: The Chosen One Fallacy
dimensions.analysis: No single person can save/redeem an entire species/organization. The "messiah" framing creates mission impossible. Distributed leadership beats heroic individual.
dimensions.metric: Leadership concentration risk - organizational resilience with key person vs. without (bus factor analysis).

vector_entry.narrative_summary: First mutant birth post-decimation. Every faction fights for her. Cable raises her in future as warrior. Messiah label creates impossible expectations. Savior and target.
vector_entry.business_logic: Succession pressure on heirs apparent. Founder's kids, Crown Prince MBS. Impossible expectations. Groomed for role but pressure toxic. Many fail or reject burden.
vector_entry.application: Succession planning, leadership development programs, heir apparent management, expectation setting, distributed leadership models

protocol_schism_split.application: Co-founder conflict resolution, organizational culture definition, values-based restructuring, spin-off strategy, peaceful dissolution frameworks
protocol_schism_split.narrative: Cyclops takes increasingly militant stance - X-Men must be soldiers, not teachers. Wolverine argues for returning to Xavier's dream of peaceful coexistence and education. Schism comes when Cyclops prepares child soldiers (generation-X students) for combat. Wolverine says no, takes students back to Westchester to reopen school. Cyclops keeps Utopia as militant base. Teams split, friends on opposite sides. Both believe they're honoring Xavier, but visions are incompatible.
protocol_schism_split.business_translation: Google founders vs. activist employees on military contracts. Coinbase CEO "no politics at work" vs. employees wanting activism. PayPal Mafia splitting into different ventures. When co-founders' values diverge, company must choose. Sometimes split is healthier than false unity. Better two viable organizations than one dysfunctional compromise.

dimensions.title: Values Misalignment Stress
dimensions.analysis: Working with someone whose values you've lost respect for is psychologically corrosive. The strain of pretending to be unified. Mental health improves post-split even if objectively harder.
dimensions.metric: Employee stress levels - cortisol, reported well-being, turnover during values conflicts vs. after resolution (split or alignment).

dimensions.title: Organizational Forking
dimensions.analysis: Like software forks - same codebase, different philosophies. React vs. Preact. Bitcoin vs. Bitcoin Cash. Each fork serves different user base better than unified compromise.
dimensions.metric: Fork viability - market share capture and satisfaction in forked entities vs. projected unified entity performance.

dimensions.title: Resource Division Economics
dimensions.analysis: Splitting resources hurts both sides short-term. But maintaining unity while fighting over resources hurts more. Sometimes divorce is efficient despite division costs.
dimensions.metric: Divorce efficiency - combined value of split entities vs. value destruction from continuing civil war.

dimensions.title: Irreconcilable Differences Exist
dimensions.analysis: Not all conflicts have compromise solutions. Some values are truly incompatible. Forcing unity creates worse outcomes than accepting incompatibility.
dimensions.metric: Compromise quality - stakeholder satisfaction with forced unity vs. clean separation when values diverge >X distance.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Cyclops (militant) vs. Wolverine (education). Child soldier debate splits team. Wolverine takes students to school, Cyclops keeps Utopia as base. Same goals, incompatible methods.
vector_entry.business_logic: Co-founder ideological split. Google military contracts. Coinbase politics debate. PayPal Mafia divergence. Sometimes split healthier than false unity.
vector_entry.application: Co-founder conflict resolution, organizational culture definition, values-based restructuring, spin-off strategy, peaceful dissolution frameworks

protocol_phoenix_five.application: Governance structure design, power distribution mechanisms, checks and balances implementation, emergency authority protocols, founder agreements
protocol_phoenix_five.narrative: Phoenix Force returns to Earth seeking Hope Summers as host. Avengers want to stop it (Phoenix = danger). X-Men want to embrace it (Phoenix = mutant salvation). Battle on moon shatters Phoenix Force into five pieces, possessing Cyclops, Emma, Namor, Colossus, Magik. Phoenix Five remake world - end hunger, war, create clean energy. But power corrupts. They become authoritarian "benevolent" dictators. Eventually Cyclops absorbs all Phoenix power, becomes Dark Phoenix, kills Professor X. Power concentration = inevitable corruption.
protocol_phoenix_five.business_translation: Multiple co-founders with equal shares seems safe - checks and balances. But during crisis, power concentrates. The CEO who "temporarily" takes emergency powers never gives them back. Board that authorizes "special measures" finds they're permanent. Even starting distributed, pressure toward concentration is immense.

dimensions.title: Power Corruption Acceleration
dimensions.analysis: Absolute power corrupts absolutely, but speed matters. Sudden power corrupts faster than gradual accumulation. Phoenix Five go from heroes to tyrants in weeks.
dimensions.metric: Corruption velocity - time from power acquisition to first abusive decision, faster with sudden vs. gradual power gain.

dimensions.title: Distributed vs. Centralized Architectures
dimensions.analysis: Blockchain's promise of distributed power vs. reality of mining concentration. "No single point of failure" until whales emerge. Distribution is unstable equilibrium.
dimensions.metric: Decentralization decay - Gini coefficient over time in supposedly distributed systems, typically trends toward concentration.

dimensions.title: Benevolent Dictator Economics
dimensions.analysis: Philosopher-king problem. Even well-intentioned autocrats create dependency, stifle markets, prevent price discovery. Phoenix Five solve world problems but make humanity dependent.
dimensions.metric: Autonomy preservation - economic independence and self-determination levels under benevolent vs. malevolent vs. absent authority.

dimensions.title: The Addiction of Doing Good
dimensions.analysis: Helping people is addictive. When you can solve any problem, you must solve every problem. Messiah complex isn't evil - it's the conviction you know what's best.
dimensions.metric: Interventionism escalation - rate at which "helping" justifications expand scope of control.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Phoenix Force splits into five X-Men. They remake world - end hunger, war. But become authoritarian. Power concentrates into Cyclops, who kills Xavier. Distributed power → concentration → corruption.
vector_entry.business_logic: Multiple co-founders with equal shares. But crisis drives concentration. CEO 'temporary' emergency powers become permanent. Distribution unstable, trends to concentration.
vector_entry.application: Governance structure design, power distribution mechanisms, checks and balances implementation, emergency authority protocols, founder agreements

protocol_krakoa_nation.business_logic: Platform Monopolies, UBI Economics & Post-Scarcity Implications
protocol_krakoa_nation.application: Platform strategy, post-scarcity economic modeling, UBI policy design, pharmaceutical pricing ethics, monopoly leverage analysis
protocol_krakoa_nation.narrative: Xavier and Magneto create Krakoan nation - sentient island offering mutants citizenship. All mutants welcome, amnesty for past crimes. Krakoa provides housing, food, teleportation via portals. In exchange, mutants manufacture miracle drugs (extending human lifespan) traded to nations for recognition. Resurrection protocols bring back all dead mutants via genetic backups and Phoenix Force. Death becomes temporary. Mutant population explodes. Creates post-scarcity economy but raises questions: What motivates people when needs are met and death is temporary?
protocol_krakoa_nation.business_translation: What happens when AI/automation creates abundance? When basic income guarantees survival? Krakoa is test case for post-work society. Also: using pharmaceutical monopoly (miracle drugs) for geopolitical leverage is exactly what pharma companies do with patents. Nations recognize Krakoa to get drugs, like recognizing China to get manufacturing.

dimensions.title: Post-Scarcity Motivation
dimensions.analysis: Maslow's hierarchy - once survival needs are met, what drives people? Creative expression? Status games? Or do they atrophy? Purpose in post-work world.
dimensions.metric: Engagement in post-scarcity - creative output, community participation when material needs are guaranteed.

dimensions.title: Resurrection Protocol Infrastructure
dimensions.analysis: Backing up consciousness, cloning bodies, reintegrating memories. The technical architecture of defeating death. Equivalent: cloud backups, redundancy, disaster recovery.
dimensions.metric: Recovery time objective - duration from death/failure to full restoration of function.

dimensions.title: Pharmaceutical Monopoly Leverage
dimensions.analysis: Control life-extension drugs = geopolitical power. Same as oil, semiconductors, rare earths. Nations will compromise values for access to crucial resources.
dimensions.metric: Resource monopoly premium - price above marginal cost that monopolist can extract based on essentiality.

dimensions.title: Death as Limitation Removal
dimensions.analysis: Death creates urgency, meaning, stakes. Without it, do choices matter? The "quantum immortality" problem - if all timelines exist, does morality matter?
dimensions.metric: Decision quality with/without stakes - when consequences are reversible, how does risk-taking change?

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Krakoan mutant nation-state. Provides housing, food, resurrection. Manufactures miracle drugs for geopolitical leverage. Post-scarcity economy. Death temporary. Questions of motivation.
vector_entry.business_logic: Platform monopolies, UBI economics, post-work society. Pharmaceutical monopoly for geopolitical power. China manufacturing leverage. What motivates people in abundance?
vector_entry.application: Platform strategy, post-scarcity economic modeling, UBI policy design, pharmaceutical pricing ethics, monopoly leverage analysis

protocol_five_resurrection.business_logic: Platform Labor & The Gig Economy of Critical Infrastructure
protocol_five_resurrection.application: Essential worker valuation, platform labor ethics, critical infrastructure resilience, service level agreement design, labor dignity in tech
protocol_five_resurrection.narrative: "The Five" are mutants whose combined powers enable resurrection: Egg (creates body), Proteus (shapes it), Elixir (adds life), Hope (boosts powers), Tempus (coordinates timing). They work shifts at "hatchery" bringing back dead mutants from genetic/memory backups. It's factory work - industrial-scale resurrection. They bring back hundreds, thousands. Creates questions: Who gets resurrected first? What about pre-backup memory loss? Is resurrected person truly "them"? Are The Five priests or factory workers?
protocol_five_resurrection.business_translation: The engineers keeping AWS running, content moderators screening trauma, delivery drivers as essential workers. They provide critical infrastructure but treated as factory workers. The Five literally hold power over life and death but work shifts. Essential labor undervalued until crisis. "Resurrection as a Service" is infrastructure-as-a-service metaphor made literal.

dimensions.title: Essential Worker Burnout
dimensions.analysis: The psychological toll of doing critical work repeatedly. Compassion fatigue in healthcare, vicarious trauma in moderators. The Five experience resurrection like assembly line.
dimensions.metric: Burnout incidence in essential workers - emotional exhaustion, depersonalization vs. other worker categories.

dimensions.title: Service Level Agreements for Life
dimensions.analysis: Resurrection becomes expectation, not miracle. SLAs on uptime. What's acceptable resurrection delay? 99.9% uptime = 8.76 hours downtime per year. Acceptable death duration?
dimensions.metric: Platform availability requirements - user tolerance for downtime on critical infrastructure services.

dimensions.title: Pricing Life & Triage Economics
dimensions.analysis: If resurrection capacity is finite, who gets priority? Payment? Status? Random? Healthcare rationing, organ transplant lists. Krakoa doesn't charge but has implicit hierarchy.
dimensions.metric: Allocation mechanisms - efficiency and equity of scarce life-saving resource distribution systems.

dimensions.title: Ship of Theseus Identity Problem
dimensions.analysis: If you replace brain cells one by one, are you still you? Clone body + implanted memories - is that the same person? What is continuity of self?
dimensions.metric: Identity continuity validation - philosophical/legal frameworks for determining "same person" status in reconstructive scenarios.

vector_entry.source_material: House of X #5, ongoing X-Men series (2019-present)
vector_entry.narrative_summary: The Five combine powers for industrial resurrection. Factory shifts bringing back dead mutants. Critical infrastructure but treated as labor. Power over life and death, working for wages.
vector_entry.business_logic: Platform essential workers. AWS engineers, content moderators, delivery drivers. Critical infrastructure undervalued. 'Resurrection as a Service' = infrastructure-as-a-service.
vector_entry.application: Essential worker valuation, platform labor ethics, critical infrastructure resilience, service level agreement design, labor dignity in tech

protocol_genosha_apartheid.application: Supply chain ethics, labor exploitation detection, forced labor elimination, human rights due diligence, systemic oppression analysis
protocol_genosha_apartheid.narrative: Genosha appears to be prosperous nation. Secret: powered by enslaved mutants. Mutants detected at birth, stripped of rights, turned into "mutates" - mind-wiped workers. They build the economy, live in camps. Government claims it's for mutants' own good - structure, purpose, safety. Eventually overthrown, becomes mutant haven, then Magneto rules it, then Sentinels genocide 16 million mutants there. The failed state cycle: oppression → revolution → chaos → authoritarianism → genocide.
protocol_genosha_apartheid.business_translation: Company towns, visa-tied foreign workers, prison labor, Uyghur forced labor. "We're giving them jobs/structure/purpose" while extracting value and removing agency. When exploitation is formalized into system, normalized. Genosha is every oppressive labor system claiming benevolence.

dimensions.title: Systemic Dehumanization
dimensions.analysis: Creating underclass requires psychological process of dehumanization. Taught that enslaved group is different, lesser, benefits from subjugation. Apartheid logic.
dimensions.metric: Dehumanization index - social distance, empathy deficit, willingness to harm outgroup vs. ingroup.

dimensions.title: Surveillance & Control Infrastructure
dimensions.analysis: Oppressive systems require technical capacity for tracking, controlling, suppressing. Genosha's mutant detection/control is advanced. Modern equivalent: China's surveillance state.
dimensions.metric: Authoritarian tech capability - surveillance density, control system sophistication vs. human rights outcomes.

dimensions.title: Exploitation-Dependent Economics
dimensions.analysis: When economy is built on cheap/slave labor, reform threatens prosperity. Resistance to change even when morally right. Southern US pre-Civil War. Gulf states today.
dimensions.metric: Economic exploitation dependence - percentage of GDP dependent on undervalued/coerced labor.

dimensions.title: The Failed State Cycle
dimensions.analysis: Oppression creates resistance. Revolution creates chaos. Chaos creates authoritarianism. Authoritarianism creates oppression. Breaking cycle requires external intervention or revolutionary wisdom (rare).
dimensions.metric: Cycle completion time - duration from oppression through revolution back to oppression (typically 1-2 generations).

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Genosha powered by enslaved mutants. Mutates mind-wiped for labor. Appears prosperous but built on oppression. Eventually overthrown, cycles through chaos to authoritarianism.
vector_entry.business_logic: Labor exploitation as 'opportunity.' Company towns, visa-tied workers, prison labor, Uyghur forced labor. System normalized. Extraction disguised as benevolence.
vector_entry.application: Supply chain ethics, labor exploitation detection, forced labor elimination, human rights due diligence, systemic oppression analysis

protocol_genosha_genocide.application: Industry transition support, workforce retraining, just transition policies, market disruption ethics, collective trauma response
protocol_genosha_genocide.narrative: Cassandra Nova sends Sentinels to Genosha. They systematically exterminate 16 million mutants in hours. Not a battle - a genocide. Sentinels are efficient, thorough, merciless. Genosha goes from mutant haven to graveyard. Few survivors. The trauma defines next generation of X-Men stories. Emma Frost survives in diamond form, surrounded by corpses. The world barely notices - 16 million mutants dead, page 12 news.
protocol_genosha_genocide.business_translation: Entire industries destroyed overnight. Blockbuster by Netflix. Taxi medallions by Uber. Coal jobs by natural gas/renewables. Kodak by digital cameras. The market doesn't mourn - it moves on. Workers in dead industries are statistics. Creative destruction is brutal for those destroyed. Survivors have PTSD. World keeps spinning.

dimensions.title: Collective Trauma & Survivor Guilt
dimensions.analysis: Genocide survivors carry permanent psychological scars. Why did I survive? Could I have saved others? The mental health crisis in post-genocide populations.
dimensions.metric: Intergenerational trauma transmission - PTSD incidence in genocide survivors and their children vs. baseline.

dimensions.title: Industrialized Killing Efficiency
dimensions.analysis: Genosha genocide used autonomous weapons. Modern equivalent: AI-enabled warfare, drone swarms. Technology makes mass killing "clean" for perpetrators.
dimensions.metric: Casualty efficiency - deaths per perpetrator hour, increases with technological sophistication.

dimensions.title: Market Indifference to Suffering
dimensions.analysis: Markets are amoral. Industry disruption creates losers but capital flows to winners. 16 million mutant deaths barely affect stock markets. Efficiency doesn't care about suffering.
dimensions.metric: Disruption empathy gap - market reaction to efficiency gains vs. humanitarian costs of disruption.

dimensions.title: Evil Banality & Automation
dimensions.analysis: Hannah Arendt's "banality of evil." Genocide doesn't require monsters - just bureaucrats following orders. Sentinels are perfect metaphor: programmed genocide, no malice.
dimensions.metric: Automation of harm - correlation between process automation and perpetrator psychological distance from consequences.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Sentinels exterminate 16 million mutants in Genosha in hours. Systematic, efficient genocide. World barely notices. Survivors traumatized. Haven to graveyard instantly.
vector_entry.business_logic: Industry extinction events. Blockbuster/Netflix, Taxis/Uber, Coal/renewables, Kodak/digital. Market doesn't mourn. Workers are statistics. Creative destruction's brutality.
vector_entry.application: Industry transition support, workforce retraining, just transition policies, market disruption ethics, collective trauma response

protocol_legacy_virus.application: Pandemic preparedness, pharmaceutical pricing policy, rare disease research funding, healthcare resource allocation, crisis sacrifice ethics
protocol_legacy_virus.narrative: Stryfe (Cable's clone) unleashes Legacy Virus - disease targeting mutants, eventual human crossover potential. Symptoms similar to AIDS. No cure initially. Mutants die slowly, publicly. Human governments delay research funding. Some humans celebrate "mutant disease." Beast races for cure but faces ethical dilemmas: human testing, triage, resource allocation. Cure eventually requires sacrifice - Colossus kills himself to release cure into atmosphere. Disease as weapon, as metaphor, as resource allocation crisis.
protocol_legacy_virus.business_translation: COVID-19 revealed every dynamic: government funding delays, treatment rationing, vaccine nationalism, price gouging, sacrifice of healthcare workers. Martin Shkreli raising drug prices 5000%. AIDS crisis funding delays. Rare disease research economics. When do we fund cures vs. let markets decide?

dimensions.title: Disease Stigma & Social Death
dimensions.analysis: Legacy Virus carriers face discrimination, isolation, fear. Social death before biological death. Same as AIDS stigma, leprosy historically. Disease becomes moral judgment.
dimensions.metric: Stigma severity - employment discrimination, social isolation, violence against disease carriers vs. actual transmission risk.

dimensions.title: Research Prioritization Algorithms
dimensions.analysis: How do we allocate research funding? Mortality? Economic impact? Political pressure? Legacy Virus delayed because mutants are minority. Rare disease problem.
dimensions.metric: Research funding equity - dollars per DALY (disability-adjusted life year) across diseases, shows political/economic bias.

dimensions.title: Pharmaceutical Pricing Power
dimensions.analysis: When cure exists but is unaffordable, market has failed. Insulin pricing. Epipen gouging. Orphan drug costs. Legacy cure required sacrifice, not payment.
dimensions.metric: Essential medicine access gap - percentage of patients who need treatment vs. percentage who can afford it.

dimensions.title: Sacrifice Ethics
dimensions.analysis: Colossus's suicide to release cure - is it noble or systemic failure that someone had to die? Should cures require martyrs? Healthcare worker COVID deaths.
dimensions.metric: Essential worker mortality premium - death rate in critical roles during crisis vs. baseline population.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Legacy Virus targets mutants, AIDS-like disease. Funding delayed, stigma severe. Beast races for cure facing ethical dilemmas. Colossus sacrifices himself to release cure.
vector_entry.business_logic: Pandemic economics. COVID, AIDS funding delays. Pharmaceutical pricing ethics. Martin Shkreli. Rare disease research. Vaccine nationalism. Healthcare worker sacrifice.
vector_entry.application: Pandemic preparedness, pharmaceutical pricing policy, rare disease research funding, healthcare resource allocation, crisis sacrifice ethics

protocol_quiet_council.application: Board composition design, stakeholder governance authenticity, ESG oversight credibility, democratic governance preservation, oligarchy prevention
protocol_quiet_council.narrative: Krakoa governed by Quiet Council - 12 mutants representing different factions (Xavier, Magneto, Apocalypse, Sinister, Emma, etc.). Consensus-based but includes literal villains. Laws passed include "Murder no man" (except humans invading Krakoa), "Make more mutants," "Respect the sacred land." Council has absolute authority but claims democratic legitimacy. Citizens have no vote. It's oligarchy with democratic aesthetics. Sinister on the council (known for genetics crimes) is like war criminals in government.
protocol_quiet_council.business_translation: Corporate boards claim stakeholder representation but are selected by existing board/CEO. ESG committees with fossil fuel execs. "Independent" directors who are friends of CEO. Facebook's oversight board. The governance theater - claiming democratic legitimacy while concentrating power. Including "reformed" bad actors because they have resources/knowledge.

dimensions.title: Oligarchic Psychology & Elite Capture
dimensions.analysis: Small groups making decisions "for" large populations develop disconnected worldview. Davos attendees solving world problems. Elite consensus ≠ popular will.
dimensions.metric: Elite-population preference gap - policy positions of decision-makers vs. constituent populations they claim to represent.

dimensions.title: Governance Theater Technology
dimensions.analysis: The technical infrastructure of fake democracy. Voting systems that don't matter. Consultation processes ignored. Comment periods performative. Algorithms creating illusion of voice.
dimensions.metric: Governance efficacy - correlation between constituent input and actual decisions made by governing body.

dimensions.title: Oligopolistic Cartel Behavior
dimensions.analysis: When council includes competitors, it's collusion. Sinister, Apocalypse, Xavier supposedly competing philosophies but coordinating. OPEC, tech companies "competing" while coordinating on labor.
dimensions.metric: Coordination evidence - price/policy correlation among supposed competitors beyond chance.

dimensions.title: Democratic Backsliding Mechanisms
dimensions.analysis: How democracies become authoritarian: concentrate power in crisis, never release it. "Emergency" becomes permanent. Krakoa founded during existential threat, emergency powers now normal.
dimensions.metric: Democratic erosion indicators - civil liberties, press freedom, electoral integrity over time under "temporary" concentrated authority.

protocol_hulk_gamma_poisoning.business_logic: Tumor evolution as intrinsic, adaptive rewiring of the host rather than an external invader. A cell that once served the organism becomes its own uncontrolled program that resists suppression. The parallel to oncology: mutations driving uncontrolled proliferation arise from the patient's own genome, and therapies that purely suppress without understanding the adaptive rewiring risk selecting for more resistant variants - the more you fight the Hulk, the stronger he gets.
protocol_hulk_gamma_poisoning.application: Oncology - tumor evolution, acquired resistance, metabolic reprogramming, clonal heterogeneity
protocol_hulk_gamma_poisoning.narrative: Bruce Banner is a scientist whose own body becomes the battlefield. Gamma radiation doesn't attack him from outside - it rewrites his cells, unleashing an uncontrolled proliferation of strength and rage that his normal physiology cannot contain. Every attempt to suppress the Hulk makes it stronger, because the Hulk is not an invader to be excised but an emergent property of Banner's own biology. The transformation is permanent, adaptive, and indistinguishable from the patient who carries it.
protocol_hulk_gamma_poisoning.business_translation:
**Dimensions**:
* D1 (Bio/Internal): Genomic Transformation
  * Logic: A driver mutation rewires cellular identity - normal cell becomes tumor cell through the same genome, not a foreign agent. Therapy must target the rewiring, not just the symptom.
  * Metric: Driver-mutation allele fraction and clonal dominance over time.

* D2 (Tech/External): Adaptive Resistance
  * Logic: External suppression selects for adaptive escape - the "Hulk getting stronger" is acquired resistance to the therapeutic pressure.
  * Metric: Time-to-progression under therapy; rise in resistance-allele frequency.

* D3 (Eco/Resources): Metabolic Rewiring
  * Logic: The transformed cell hijacks nutrient resources (glycolysis, angiogenesis) to fuel uncontrolled growth, like the Hulk consuming energy for rage.
  * Metric: Metabolic reprogramming score; glycolytic flux; tumor vascular density.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Identity Collapse
  * Logic: The boundary between healthy host and disease collapses - the tumor is the patient, making "us vs. them" oncology models incomplete.
  * Metric: Tumor-normal genomic relatedness; clonal heterogeneity index.

protocol_xmen_cancer_genes.business_logic: Cancer predisposition and oncogene activation as latent potential requiring a trigger. Germline risk variants lie dormant until a somatic event activates them; the immune system and microenvironment decide whether a transformed cell is a threat; and fear of the "cancer gene" can stigmatize carriers regardless of actual risk. The parallel to oncology: tumor-suppressor loss and oncogene activation are about latency, triggers, and surveillance - not inevitability.
protocol_xmen_cancer_genes.application: Oncology - germline risk, oncogene activation, immunoediting, cancer prevention, tumor microenvironment
protocol_xmen_cancer_genes.narrative: Every mutant carries a dormant X-gene. For most it never activates; for others it erupts into power - sometimes a gift, sometimes a curse. The mutant must learn whether the gene is destiny or choice, and whether to use, hide, or fight its expression. Society fears what the gene might become, even when it never activates. The mutation is not evil in itself - it is potential, and the outcome depends on triggers, environment, and whether the carrier integrates or is suppressed.
protocol_xmen_cancer_genes.business_translation:
**Dimensions**:
* D1 (Bio/Internal): Latent Oncogenic Potential
  * Logic: Germline risk variants and proto-oncogenes remain dormant until a somatic trigger (mutation, inflammation) activates them.
  * Metric: Variant penetrance; time-to-activation; oncogenic trigger burden.

* D2 (Tech/External): Surveillance & Immune Gatekeeping
  * Logic: The immune system and microenvironment decide whether an activated gene becomes a tumor - "society's response to the mutant."

protocol_venom_symbiote.business_logic: The tumor-microenvironment relationship and intratumoral heterogeneity. A tumor and its surrounding stroma co-evolve into a single adapted ecosystem where the boundary between "host tissue" and "tumor" blurs, and aggressive surgical or therapeutic extraction can fail because the tumor has co-opted and is sustained by the surrounding tissue. The parallel to oncology: the tumor is not an isolated mass but a bonded system with its microenvironment - targeting the bond, not just the mass, is the therapeutic lever.
protocol_venom_symbiote.application: Oncology - tumor microenvironment, stroma, combination therapy, intratumoral heterogeneity, resistance
protocol_venom_symbiote.narrative: A host and a symbiote form a bond that makes them stronger together - but the symbiote also invades, suppresses the host's will, and cannot be cleanly removed without risk of death or damage to both. The longer they are bonded, the harder it is to tell where the host ends and the invader begins. Attempts to tear them apart often make things worse, because the two have become a single adapted system.

  * Metric: Extracellular matrix remodeling; vascular co-option; immune suppression markers.

  * Logic: Tumor and stroma share nutrients and signals in a bonded economy - neither is self-sufficient alone.
  * Metric: Nutrient flux at tumor-stroma boundary; paracrine signaling density.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Indivisible Adaptation
  * Logic: Host and tumor become a single system; clean separation is impossible, demanding a systems-level therapeutic approach.
  * Metric: Co-dependency score; response to combination (not monotherapy) strategies.

protocol_dormammu_bargain.business_logic: Defeating a dominant, resource-abundant adversary (like an aggressive tumor) not by out-powering it but by changing the structure of the conflict - a scheduling or fractionation strategy that makes the adversary's advantage unsustainable. The parallel to oncology: treatment scheduling (fractionated dosing, adaptive therapy, therapy-free holidays) can convert an unwinnable arms race against a fast-evolving tumor into a sustainable stalemate, trading cure-for-now for control-over-time.
protocol_dormammu_bargain.application: Oncology - adaptive therapy, fractionation, treatment scheduling, therapy holidays, resistance management
protocol_dormammu_bargain.narrative: Doctor Strange cannot defeat Dormammu with force - the Dark Dimension lord is too powerful. Instead, Strange traps Dormammu in a repeating time loop, forcing the eternal being to relive the same moment of confrontation forever. Dormammu, who has infinite power but not infinite patience, eventually agrees to a bargain: he leaves Earth, trading his conquest for an end to the unbearable loop. Victory comes not from matching force with force, but from changing the structure of the conflict.
protocol_dormammu_bargain.business_translation:

* D1 (Bio/Internal): Evolutionary Arms Race
  * Logic: The tumor has more "power" (proliferative capacity) than any single therapy can match with force.
  * Metric: Tumor growth rate; clonal fitness landscape.

* D2 (Tech/External): Treatment Scheduling as Structure
  * Logic: Changing the schedule (not the drug) alters the conflict structure - fractionation, adaptive dosing, therapy holidays.
  * Metric: Time-to-resistance under adaptive vs. continuous dosing; progression-free survival.

* D3 (Eco/Resources): Resource-Driven Stalemate
  * Logic: A sustainable treatment strategy conserves patient resources and delays exhaustion vs. a costly arms race.
  * Metric: Toxicity-adjusted survival; cumulative treatment burden; quality-adjusted life years.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Sustainable Control over Cure
  * Logic: When cure is unreachable, the goal shifts to an indefinite sustainable stalemate - control-over-time.
  * Metric: Chronic disease control duration; time to symptomatic progression.

protocol_deadpool_regeneration.business_logic: The therapeutic paradox where a tumor-associated pathway is essential to host survival. Some treatments target a pathway the patient depends on (like a mutated cancer-adjacent survival signal), where removing the disease removes the patient. The parallel to oncology: on-target-on-tumor toxicity, pathways that are both oncogenic and essential, and the reality that some patients live with chronic, controllable disease rather than full elimination - the cancer is not separable from the patient's continued existence.
protocol_deadpool_regeneration.application: Oncology - on-target-on-tumor toxicity, essential pathways, chronic disease control, therapeutic index
protocol_deadpool_regeneration.narrative: Wade Wilson was a mercenary dying of cancer. The experimental Weapon X treatment did not cure him - it mutated his cancer cells into an aggressive healing factor. Now his body regenerates from almost any wound, but the cancer is never gone; it is fused with his vitality. His immortality and his disease are the same thing. He lives only because his tumors sustain him, and any attempt to remove the "disease" would kill the "patient."

  * Metric: On-target-on-tumor toxicity; therapeutic index; essentiality score.

  * Logic: The therapeutic intervention itself (the treatment) can transform the disease - creating the very immortality it sought.
  * Metric: Therapy-induced secondary malignancy; treatment-related mutation burden.

* D3 (Eco/Resources): Chronic Coexistence
  * Logic: The patient lives WITH the disease, sustained by it - an economy of chronic coexistence rather than elimination.
  * Metric: Chronic disease control; quality-adjusted survival; treatment-free interval.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Inseparable Vitality
  * Logic: Removing the disease would remove the patient - a hard limit on curative intent.
  * Metric: Survival without the targetable pathway; dependency on the oncogenic mechanism.

protocol_phoenix_force.archetype: Dual Cosmic Force / Potent Unregulated Therapy
protocol_phoenix_force.business_logic: The double-edged nature of powerful therapies - immunotherapies, cell therapies, and targeted agents that can cure or kill depending on control and regulation. The same immune activation that eradicates a tumor can, unregulated, become a cytokine storm or autoimmunity that destroys the patient (the "Dark Phoenix" of on-target toxicity). The parallel to oncology: powerful immune- and cell-based therapies require regulatory control to avoid trading one destruction (the tumor) for another (the patient).
protocol_phoenix_force.application: Oncology - immunotherapy, CAR-T, cytokine release syndrome, on-target toxicity, oncolytic therapy
protocol_phoenix_force.narrative: The Phoenix is a cosmic entity of creation and destruction that chooses a host to manifest through. In Jean Grey, it grants incredible power - resurrection, healing, telekinesis - but the same force, when the host is overwhelmed, becomes the Dark Phoenix, annihilating worlds. The power is not evil; it is unchecked potential without regulation. The difference between savior and destroyer is whether the host can integrate the force or is consumed by it.

  * Metric: Objective response rate; depth of response; tumor cell kill.

* D2 (Tech/External): Unregulated Toxicity
  * Logic: The same force, uncontrolled, becomes the Dark Phoenix - cytokine release syndrome, autoimmunity, neurotoxicity.
  * Metric: CRS severity grade; immune-related adverse events; on-target-off-tumor toxicity.

* D3 (Eco/Resources): Resource of Life and Death
  * Logic: The force is a shared resource that heals or destroys depending on how it is channeled and dosed.
  * Metric: Therapeutic window; dose-limiting toxicity; risk-benefit ratio.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Host Integration or Consumption
  * Logic: Whether the patient integrates the powerful therapy or is consumed by it decides cure vs. catastrophe.
  * Metric: Durable remission with tolerable toxicity; treatment-related mortality.

protocol_skrull_infiltration.business_logic: Cancer's ability to evade detection by disguising itself as normal tissue and subverting the body's own defenses. Tumors down-regulate antigens, recruit regulatory cells, and masquerade as self to escape immune surveillance - the enemy is already inside, indistinguishable from healthy tissue. The parallel to oncology: immune evasion, checkpoint activation, and tumor disguise demand verification (biomarkers, liquid biopsy, imaging) to expose the hidden threat that conventional "self-recognition" cannot catch.
protocol_skrull_infiltration.application: Oncology - immune evasion, biomarkers, liquid biopsy, minimal residual disease, tumor disguise, surveillance
protocol_skrull_infiltration.narrative: The Skrulls don't attack from without - they have spent years replacing humans, one by one, with perfect replicas. No one knows who is real. Allies cannot be trusted, institutions are compromised, and the only defense is relentless verification of everyone's identity. The war is not a battle against an external army but an internal security crisis where the enemy wears the face of the defender.

  * Metric: Antigen presentation loss; neoantigen burden; immune-evasion phenotype.

* D2 (Tech/External): Detection & Verification
  * Logic: Because the enemy is disguised, continuous verification (biomarkers, ctDNA, imaging) is the primary defense.
  * Metric: Detection sensitivity/specificity; minimal-residual-disease detection rate.

* D3 (Eco/Resources): Subverted Infrastructure
  * Logic: The tumor subverts the body's own infrastructure (vasculature, immune cells) into supporting the disguise.
  * Metric: Regulatory T-cell / MDSC infiltration; checkpoint ligand expression.

* D4 (Cosmic/Limit): Trust Erosion
  * Logic: The impossibility of trusting 'self' erodes the host's defensive assumption - constant surveillance becomes necessary.
  * Metric: Recurrence detection lead time; surveillance intensity; false-positive burden.
